chapter: Recording with King Oliver and Clarence Williams
title: The 'Snag It' record and the Aunt Hagar's Blues arrangement
summary: Waters says he bought a record of himself on 'Snag It' in Europe and that Panassie wrongly credited Bigard on 'Aunt Hagar's Blues', which he both played and arranged for Clarence Williams.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, it's not unlisted in the record that I bought, 'cause I bought the record -
You have a record of yourself playing 'Snag It' with -
I bought the record, I bought the record in, I don't know where it is now but I bought the record in Europe.
You have a record of yourself playing 'Snag It' with King Oliver?

Yeah. I've all, I don't know where I can find it, but I bought it, I bought it in a department store. That's, it's - and the names is diff - you can't go by the books always, I tell you why. Well, I -
I know records that are issued fairly well and I -
with Benny Waters on it with King Oliver, and that you're saying the record exists -
Yeah, yeah. That's the only [ ] song that I knew of all those 6 sides that I did, I mean 6 sessions.

I give you the idea who I worked with then - I mean, that'll help you out too, see. Why I say you can't always go by the books, I mean because Hugues Panassie had Barney Bigard makin' 'Aunt Hagar's Blues'. And I made it, not only did I make the record, I made the arrangement for Clarence Williams, see what I'm talkin' about?
See, so you can't always, you kind of get mixed up, but -
Wait a second, now, this is listed. There are rejected Brunswick dates, look, in the summer of 1927, the fall of 1927 -
and there's 'Aunt Hagar's Blues' in the book has your arrangement credited.
He didn't, in this book that he had -
He said Barney Bigard made the record, you see?
I told him 'bout it before he died. See, I wrote him and told him, I said 'You made a mistake there, Hugues'. I said 'Not only did I make the record, I made the arrangement'.
